senses: to bring or collect together, gather; unite, join, connect
to bring or place together or near, set in opposition, oppose, match; bring into hostile contact
to bring together for comparison, compare, contrast
to consult, confer, consider, deliberate, talk over, discuss; exchange (words)
to compress, abridge, condense, sum up
to bear, carry, convey, direct, take, bring
to collect money, treasures, etc., for any object, bring offerings, contribute
to devote, apply to, employ, use, direct, bestow upon, confer, grant
to pay in, contribute, be profitable, be of use
la:verb:confero.html:
confĕro, contŭli, collātum (conl-), conferre, v. a.
To bring, bear, or carry together, to collect, gather (freq. and class.).
In gen.: ligna circa casam,: arma,: cibos ore suo (aves),: undique collatis membris,: sarcinas in unum locum,; cf. : collatis militaribus signis,: ut premerer sacrā Lauroque collatāque myrto,: quo (sc. in proximum horreum) omne rusticum instrumentum,: illuc (sc. in castella) parentes et conjuges,: dentes in corpore (canes),: materiam omnem, antequam dicere ordiamur,: summas (scriptorum) in commentarium et capita,: plura opera in unam tabulam,: quae in proximos quinque libros conlata sunt,: res Romanas Graeco peregrinoque sermone in historiam, Just. pr. 1; cf. ; cf. I. B. 5. infra.; : rogus inimicis collatus manibus,—
In partic.
To collect money, treasures, etc., for any object, to bring offerings, contribute: dona mihi,: contulit aes populus,; so freq. on monuments: AERE CONLATO,; ; : EX AERE CONLATO,: aurum argentumque in publicum,: munera ei,: tributa quotannis ex censu,: conferre eo minus tributi,: in commune,; : quadringena talenta quotannis Delum,: (pecunia) ad ejus honores conlata,: ad honorem tuum pecunias maximas contulisse,: sextantes in capita,: pecunias,; ; ; : vinum alius, alius mel,; pr.: sua bona in medium, pr.: magnam partem patrimonii alicui rei,: cum et Socrati collatum sit ad victum,.—Absol.: nos dabimus, nos conferemus, nostro sumptu, non tuo,.—Hence,
Trop., like the Gr. συμφέρω (v. Lidd. and Scott in h. v. 5.), to be useful, profitable, to profit, serve, be of use to ( = prosum; cf. also conduco, II.; post-Aug., and only in the third person; most freq. in Quint.); constr. with ad, in, the dat., inf., or absol.
With ad: naturane plus ad eloquentiam conferat an doctrina,; so ; ; ; ; , prooem. § 6; .—*
With in: rursus in alia plus prior (exercitatio) confert,.—
With dat.: Gracchorum eloquentiae multum contulisse matrem,; so id. prooem. § 6; 2, 9, 2; 3, 7, 12 al.; ; ; ; .—
With subj. inf.: incipiente incremento confert alterna folia circum obruere,.—(ε) Absol.: multum veteres etiam Latini conferunt, imprimis copiam verborum,; ; ; cf. Sillig ad .—
To bring into connection, to unite, join, connect: membris collatis, of an embrace,; cf. ora,: fontes e quibus collatae aquae flumen emittunt,: capita, to lay heads together (in conferring, deliberating, etc.), ; : pedem, to go or come with one, ; so, gradum ( = congredi),; ; .—Of chemical union: dissimiles et dispares res in unam potestatem,.—
Trop.: collatis viribus,; cf.: conferre vires in unum,: collata omnium vota in unius salutem,: e singulis frustis collata oratio,; cf. : velut studia inter nos conferebamus,.— So esp. of conferences, consultations, etc., to consult together, confer, consider or talk over together: si quid res feret, coram inter nos conferemus,: sollicitudines nostras inter nos,: rationes,: familiares sermones cum aliquo, to unite in familiar conversation with, : cum hoc in viā sermonem contulit,; cf.: cum aliquo aut sermones aut consilia,: consilia ad adulescentes,; cf.: consilia dispersim antea habita,: injurias,to deliberate together concerning,; Cael. ap. .— Absol.: omnes sapientes decet conferre et fabulari,.—With a rel.clause: fusi contulerimus inter nos ... quid finis,: ibi conferentibus, quid animorum Hispanis esset,.—
To bring or join together in a hostile manner, to set together (most freq. in milit. lang.): (Galli) cum Fontejo ferrum ac manus contulerunt, (1, 2): signa cum Alexandrinis,; cf.: collatis signis depugnare,; : arma cum aliquo,; ; cf.: arma inter se,: castra cum hoste,; cf.: castra castris,; ; ; : pedem cum pede,to fight foot to foot,; cf.: pede conlato,; ; : gradum cum aliquo,: pectora luctantia nexu pectoribus,: stat conferre manum Aeneae,: prima movet Cacus collatā proelia dextrā,: collatis cursibus hastas conicere,: seque viro vir contulit,.—Poet.: inter sese duri certamina belli,: contra conferre manu certamina pugnae,: collato Marte,.—Absol.: mecum confer, ait,fight with me,.—
Transf. from milit. affairs to lawsuits: pedem, to encounter, come in contact with one, to attack: non possum magis pedem conferre, ut aiunt, aut propius accedere?: pedem cum singulis,; cf. ; cf.: qui illi concedi putem utilius esse quod postulat quam signa conferri,.—Poet.: lites,to contend, quarrel,.—
To bring together for comparison, to compare; constr. with cum, inter se, ad, the dat., or acc. only.
With cum: quem cum eo (sc. Democrito) conferre possumus non modo ingenii magnitudine sed etiam animi?; so : ut non conferam vitam neque existimationem tuam cum illius,, § 45; : cum maximis minima,; ; : nostras leges cum illorum Lycurgo et Dracone et Solone,; cf.: illa cum Graeciā,; v. also δ. —
With inter se (rare): vitam inter se utriusque conferte,.— *
With ad: bos ad bovem collatus, Müll.—
With dat.: tempora praesentia praeteritis,: parva magnis,: alicui illud,: lanam tinctam Tyriae lacernae,: ingenia ingeniis,: illam puellis,; : nil jucundo amico,: (Pausanias et Lysander) ne minimā quidem ex parte Lycurgi legibus et disciplinae conferendi sunt,; cf. supra, α.—(ε) With acc. only: tesseram hospitalem,: conferte Verrem: non ut hominem cum homine comparetis, etc.,: exemplum,; ; : nec cum quaereretur gener Tarquinio, quisquam Romanae juventutis ullā arte conferri potuit,; : census,.—Of documents: haec omnia summā curā et diligentiā recognita et conlata sunt,.—
With the idea of shortening by bringing together (cf. colligo), to compress, abridge, condense, make or be brief: quam potero in verba conferam paucissima,; cf.: in pauca, ut occupatus nunc sum, confer, quid velis,: rem in pauca,; and: in pauca verba,; id: : totam Academiam ... ex duobus libris contuli in quattuor,: ut in pauca conferam,: sua verba in duos versus,: ex immensā diffusāque legum copiā optima quaeque et necessaria in paucissimos libros,.—

*

To join in bringing forward, to propose unitedly (as a law; cf. fero, II. B. 8. b.): cur enim non confertis, ne sit conubium divitibus et pauperibus, Weissenb. ad loc.
(Con intens.) To bear, carry, convey, direct a thing somewhere (in haste, for protection, etc.); and conferre se, to betake or turn one's self anywhere, to go (very freq. and class.).
Prop.
In gen.
With the designation of the goal: quo me miser conferam? Gracch. ap. : qui cum se suaque omnia in oppidum Bratuspantium contulissent,: se suaque eo,: se suaque in naves,: iter Brundisium versus,; cf.: iter eo, Brut. ap. : suas rationes et copias in illam provinciam,: legiones in mediam aciem, Auct. B. Alex. 39; Auct. B. Afr. 60: quos eodem audita Cannensis clades contulerat,: parentes illuc,: se Rhodum conferre,: se Laodiceam, Lent. ap. : se Colonas,: quo se fusa acies,: se ad Tissaphernem,; so, se ad Pharnabazum,: se in fugam,: sese in pedes, Enn. ap. ; (cf.: conicere se in pedes,).—Of things: pituita eo se umorve confert,.—
Absol.: pulcre haec confertur ratis,is borne away,.—
Esp., in (cf. abeo, II.): aliquem in aliquid, to change into, transform to something: aliquem in saxum,: versos vultus (poet. circumlocution for se) in hanc, : corpus in albam volucrem,.—
Trop.
In gen., to bring, turn, direct something to; and conferre se, to turn, apply, devote one's self to, etc.: quo mortuo me ad pontificem Scaevolam contuli,: (Crassus) cum initio aetatis ad amicitiam se meam contulisset,; : qui se ad senatūs auctoritatem, ad libertatem vestram contulerunt,; : se ad studium scribendi,: se ad studia litterarum,; cf. : meus pater eam seditionem in tranquillum conferet (the figure taken from the sea when in commotion),: verba ad rem, to bring words to actions, i. e. to pass from words to deeds, ; : suspitionem in Capitonem,: ut spes votaque sua non prius ad deos quam ad principum aures conferret,: lamentationes suas etiam in testamentum,.—More freq., in partic.,
With the access. idea of application or communication, to devote or apply something to a certain purpose, to employ, direct, confer, bestow upon, give, lend, grant, to transfer to (a favorite word with Cic.).
With dat.: dona quid cessant mihi Conferre?: tibi munera,; : victoribus praemia,: puellae quinquaginta milia nummūm,: fructum alio,; .—
With ad and acc.: hostiles exuvias ornatum ad urbis et posterum gloriam,: Mithridates omne reliquum tempus non ad oblivionem veteris belli, sed ad comparationem novi contulit,: omne studium atque omne ingenium ad populi Romani gloriam laudemque celebrandam,; : omnem meam curam atque operam ad philosophiam,: omnem tuum amorem omnemque tuam prudentiam ... confer ad eam curam,: animum ad fodiendos puteos, Auct. B. Alex. 9: ad naturae suae non vitiosae genus consilium vivendi omne,: orationem omnem ad misericordiam,.—
With in: omnes curas cogitationesque in rem publicam,: diligentiam in valetudinem tuam,: praedas ac manubias suas non in monumenta deorum immortalium, neque in urbis ornamenta conferre, sed, etc.,: in eos, quos speramus nobis profuturos, non dubitamus officia conferre,; so, plurimum benignitatis in eum,; : curam restituendi Capitolii in L. Vestinum confert, i. e. assigns to, charges with, : in unius salutem collata omnium vota,.—
With erga: commemoratio benevolentiae ejus, quam erga me a pueritiā contulisses,.—
With aliquid ad or in aliquem or aliquid, to refer or ascribe something to a person or thing as its possessor, author (in a good, and freq. in a bad sense), to attribute, impute, assign, ascribe to one, to lay to the charge of: species istas hominum in deos,: res ad imperium deorum,: permulta in Plancium, quae ab eo numquam dicta sunt, conferuntur ... Stomachor vero, cum aliorum non me digna in me conferuntur,; : mortis illius invidiam in L. Flaccum,: suum timorem in rei frumentariae simulationem angustiasque itinerum,: sua vitia et suam culpam in senectutem,: hanc ego de re publicā disputationem in Africani personam et Phili contuli,.—So esp.: culpam in aliquem,; ; , a, 1: causam in aliquem,; ; cf.: causam in tempus,.—
To transfer to a fixed point of time, fix, assign, refer, appoint, put off, defer, postpone (cf. differo): Carthaginis expugnationem in hunc annum,: in posterum diem iter suum contulit, Brut. ap. : omnia in mensem Martium,: aliquid in ambulationis tempus,: eam pecuniam in rei publicae magnum aliquod tempus,: quod in longiorem diem conlaturus fuisset,: alicujus consulatum in annum aliquem,.—Rarely of place: idoneum locum in agris nactus ... ibi adventum expectare Pompei eoque omnem belli rationem conferre constituit,—
To bring on, cause, occasion, induce: pestem alicui,: candorem mollitiamque,.

la:verb:confirmo.gloss: to make firm, establish, re-establish, strengthen, fortify, mature, confirm
senses: to make firm, establish, re-establish, strengthen, fortify, mature, confirm
to demonstrate, corroborate, support, prove or confirm the truth of something; assert, affirm
la:verb:confirmo.html:
con-firmo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to make firm, establish, strengthen, confirm (class., esp. in prose).
In gen. (prop. and trop.): stipites confirmare et stabilire,: ali hōc vires nervosque confirmari putant,: dentis mobilis,; cf. ; sq.: confirmare et densare defluentem capillum,: crus debile,; cf. : maxime religando confirmant parietum soliditatem,: castellum magnis munitionibus multisque tormentis, Auct. B. Alex. 21, 5: intestina,i. e. to heal, cure,: cicatriculam,: se, to recover physically, to grow well (corresp. with convalescere), ; ; ; 16, 1, 1.—Transf., of the vine, : valetudinem,: pacem et amicitiam cum proximis civitatibus,; cf.: confirmare societatem datā ac acceptā fide,: opes factionis,; cf.: viris suas,: suam manum,: se transmarinis auxiliis,: conjurationem,: regnum Persarum,; so, regnum,: imperium,: decreta,to confirm,: acta Caesaris,, C, 12: acta alicujus in transmarinis provinciis,: beneficia edicto,: provinciam a Caesare datam,.—
Esp.
To confirm or strengthen courage, to instil courage into one, to encourage, inspirit, animate, embolden: animum meum,to take heart, take courage,: animum sapientissimi hominis,; : maximi animi hominem,: animos ratione,: confirmare et excitare afflictos animos bonorum,: animos Gallorum verbis,; : vacillantium gentium animos,: suos ad dimicandum animo,: milites,: timentes,; cf.: diffidentem rebus suis,: territos,: perterritos,; : Massilienses obsidione laborantes adventu suo,: animum suum ad virtutem, Klotz (al. conformavit): nepotem suum ad successionem imperii,: nunc erige te et confirma,take courage,: cum ipse te confirmasses,hast acquired courage,; cf.: confirmant ipsi se,; ; : eos multa pollicendo confirmat, uti Romam pergerent,: alius alium confirmare, ne nomina darent,.—Aliquem alicui rei: gladiatores Lentulus libertati confirmat, encourages them to freedom, i. e. incites them to make themselves worthy of freedom, dub. (Dinter and Kraner: spe libertatis).—With abstr. objects: reliqui temporis spem,: spem alicujus,: suspitionem,; cf.: sensus rectus et confirmatus,.—
To confirm one in his disposition or feelings, in his fidelity (rare): insulas bene animatas,: homines,: Gallias,.—
To confirm, give full assurance of, a fact, corroborate an assertion, settle, fix, establish, to prove, demonstrate the truth of a thing, etc. (very freq.): confirmare nostra argumentis ac rationibus, deinde contraria refutare,; so opp. refutare,; 5, 13, 53; cf. opp. refellere,; ; opp. diluere,: confirmare aut infirmare rem,: divinationem,; cf. : quorum omnium testimoniis de hac Dionis pecuniā confirmatum est,: crimen commenticium,: haec istius vituperatio atque infamia confirmabatur eorum sermone, qui, etc.,: perjurium,, § 19: iste locus est tibi etiam atque etiam confirmandus,: his rebus confirmatis, Kraner ad loc. —With acc. and inf., ; cf. ,

179; 5, 198.—Pass. impers., with ne: sanctissimo jurejurando confirmari oportere, ne tecto recipiatur, qui non, etc.,: hoc idem visum esse ex superioribus castellis confirmaverunt,; cf.: hoc ex ipsis caeli rationibus ausim Confirmare, nequaquam esse creatam, etc.,.—Hence,

To assert, affirm, protest something as true or certain; constr. with acc., acc. and inf., or de: hoc cum mihi non modo confirmasset, sed etiam persuasisset,: talem exsistere eloquentiam non potuisse confirmo,.—So with acc. and inf., ; cf.: illud se polliceri et jurejurando confirmare, tutum iter per fines suos daturum,: confirmare, fidem publicam per sese inviolatam fore,: memini me audire te de glorioso et celeri reditu meo confirmare,.—So with de, ; .—Hence, confirmātus, a, um, P. a.
(In acc. with II. A.) Encouraged, courageous, resolute: animus certus et confirmatus,; so, sensus rectus et confirmatus,: confirmatiorem exercitum efficere,.—
(Acc. to II. C.) Asserted, affirmed: in quibus (litteris) erat confirmatius idem illud, etc.,.—
(Proved; hence,) Certain, credible: quod eo confirmatius erit, si, etc.,: fides confirmatissima, most fixed, Porph. ad .—* Adv.: confirmātē (in acc. with I.), firmly, .

la:verb:confugio.html:
con-fŭgĭo, fūgi, 3,
v. n., to flee to forrefuge or succor, take refuge in or with (class. in prose and poetry).
Prop.: ad me nocte primā domum,; cf.: ad aliquem,; ; ; ; : huc,: in naves,: in arcem,; : in aram,; cf.: ad aram,: Peliae ad limina supplex,: ad ipsos deos,: ad fana deorum, Gai ; : ad vestras manus. ad vestra arma,: Phylen,: Perusiam,.—
Trop., to take refuge in, have recourse to (esp. freq. in Cic.): ad opem judicum,; cf.: ad florentes Etruscorum opes,: ad meam fidem,: ad clementiam tuam,: ad preces,; ; : ad artes patrias,: cujus (philosophiae) in sinum,: in tuam fidem, veritatem, misericordiam,: quasi ad aram in exsilium,: neque tu scilicet Eo nunc confugies: Quid mea, etc.? to take refuge, i. e. excuse yourself with, ; cf.: an illuc confugies,: Epicurus confugit illuc, ut neget, etc.,: habebam quo confugerem, ubi conquiescerem,: confugiet ad imprudentiam, stultitiam, adulescentiam,.—Impers.: confugitur aliquo,; .

la:verb:conficio.gloss: to prepare, accomplish, complete, execute; settle, close a bargain; traverse
senses: to prepare, accomplish, complete, execute; settle, close a bargain; traverse
to produce, cause, bring about, effect, secure
to finish, end, spend, pass, complete
to procure, bring together, collect, produce, prepare
to diminish, lessen, wear out, consume, exhaust
la:verb:conficio.html:
confĭcĭo, fēci, fectum, 3 (
perf. subj. confexim, ; in pass., besides the regular form conficior, freq., but not in Cic., in acc. with fīo, fieri: confit,; ; ; ; ; ; ; : confiunt,; : confiat,; Lachm.: confiant, Imp. Leo, Cod. 2, 7, 11: confieret, Balb. ap. , A, 3; 9, 7, A, 1; : confierent,; : confieri,; ; ; Sulp. ap. ; ; v. Forbig. ad loc.; ; cf. Neue, Formenl. II. p. 611), v. a.
facio
.
To make a thing completely ready, to make, prepare, bring about, complete, accomplish, execute, etc. (except in Quint., freq. in all periods and species of composition).
Lit.
In gen.: nisi cottidiano sesquiopus confeceris,; cf. pensum,; : eme lanam, unde pallium conficiatur,; cf.: anulum, pallium, soccos suā manu,: vestem,; : ligna ad fornacem,to make ready, prepare for,; cf.: conficere atque contexere villos ovium,: aurum et argentum,: frumenta (with molere),: tabulas litteris Graecis,to write, draw up,;

cf.: libros Graeco sermone,to compose, write,; and librum Graece,: tabulas,: orationes,: illam partem superiorem orationis,: nuptias,; : bellum,; ; Vatin. ap. ; ; so, duella,; cf. proelium,: tantum facinus,; cf. caedem,: legitima quaedam,: residua diurni actus,: mandata,; ; (14), 3; : omnibus rebus magnā curā, multā operā et labore confectis,, B, 8: ad eas res conficiendas biennium sibi satis esse ducere,: negotium,; : quibus rebus confectis,; ; : confecto legationis officio,.—

Esp.
In the lang. of business, to settle, close a bargain, finish, etc.; absol.: tu cum Apellā Chio confice de columnis,: quod si mihi permisisses, confecissem cum coheredibus,: de Acutiliano negotio quod mihi mandaras ... confeceram,.—
Of space or distance traversed, to pass over, accomplish, traverse, go over, make, accomplish: iter,; ; ; cf.: tertiam partem itineris,; and poet.: nos immensum spatiis confecimus aequor,: cursum,; : cursum vitae,: cursus annuos conficit sol,; : longam viam,: celeritate incredibili longissimas vias,.—Rarely of space occupied: tecta facturi, ut mille passuum conficiatur, (14).—
Trop.
In gen., to produce, cause, make, bring about, effect: sollicitudines mihi,: geminas nuptias,; cf.: aliquid mali gnato,: pacem,: motus animorum,.—With two accs.: animum auditoris mitem et misericordem,: reditum alicui,to procure,.—Also absol., to be efficient, to accomplish a direct result, be an active cause (philos. t. t.): aliae causae ipsae conficiunt, aliae vim aliquam ad conficiendum afferunt,.—
Of time, to complete, finish, end, spend, pass: cum sexaginta annos confecerit,: centum annos,: diem,: tum denique judicetur beatusne fuerit, cum extremum vitae diem morte confecerit,: annuum tempus,: omnem vitae suae cursum in labore corporis atque in animi contentione (just before: ut in amore et voluptatibus adulescentiam suam collocaret),: annuum munus,: biennium,: suas horas (somnus),: aequinoctium,; cf. brumam,; : commissum ac profligatum bellum,; .—
In philos. lang., to bring forward as proved, to show, deduce: conclusio est, quae ex eis quae ante dicta sunt, conficit, quid necessario consequatur,; ; hence, conficior, to follow logically (from something), to be deduced; with ex: cum id perspicuum sit, quod conficiatur ex ratiocinatione,; so ; ; ; and absol., —
Transf., to diminish, lessen, weaken an object; to sweep away, destroy, kill, wear out, consume.
Prop.: dentes intimi escas conficiunt,grind,; so ; ; cf. cibos,to digest,; : ignes Conficerent vulgo silvas, arbusta cremarent,; cf.: conficere, omnia igni, frigore,: patrimonium suum (corresp. with dissipare),: sapiens si fame ipse conficiatur ... vir bonus, ne ipse frigore conficiatur, etc.,.—With acc. and inf.: ipse conficior venisse tempus cum possim, etc.,: nihil est opere et manu factum, quod non conficiat et consumat vetustas,: quae vetustas est, quae vim divinam conficere possit? .—In part. perf.: sicut fortis equus ... senio confectu' quiescit, impaired, weakened, Enn. ap. ; and so very freq.: confectus senectute,: aetate,; : aevo,: senectā, Ov M. 6, 37: cum corporis morbo tum animi dolore,; cf. ; : multis gravibusque vulneribus,; ; : curā,: dolore,.—Without abl.: ut fessos confectosque aggrediantur,exhausted,; cf.: confectus et saucius,: artus,: ego te hic hac offatim conficiam,to cut in pieces,: Athenienses,to subdue,; so, provinciam,; ; ; ; 41, 12, 3; cf. ; ; : duos hostium exercitus,: me (sica illa) paene confecit,killed,: alterum Curiatium,; cf. saucium,: Caligulam vulneribus triginta,: maximam vim serpentium (ibes),; so of the killing of animals,; ; ; cf. confector, II.; and in mal. part., (v. the passage in its connection).—
Trop.: conficere aliquem verbis,: (captivos) omnibus notis ignominiisque,: lectio non cruda sed multa iteratione mollita et velut confecta,: sidus confectum,its influence has ceased, it has set,; .—
In gen., to prepare, provide, procure, to bring together, = colligo: virginem, Quam amabat, eam confeci sine molestiā, Ruhnk.; so, centurias,to secure their votes,; cf.: suam tribum necessariis suis,: hortos mihi,: bibliothecam,fin.: exercitum difficili rei publicae tempore,: exercitus maximos,; cf.: armata milia centum,: (serpentum) magnam multitudinem (just before, colligere),: erat ei de ratiunculā apud me pauxillulum nummorum, id ut conficerem: confeci,: permagnam pecuniam ex illā re,; cf.: conficiendae pecuniae rationes,.—Hence, confĭcĭ-ens, entis, P. a. (acc. to I.), effecting, causing, producing, efficient (rare, and only in Cic.): causae,: corporis bonorum conficientia (τἁ τῶν ἀγαθῶν ποιητικά), productive of physical good, Madv.: civitas conficientissima litterarum,very carefully noting down every thing,.

la:verb:confido.gloss: to be confident or assured of, confide in, believe, trust, place or put confidence in; rely upon
senses: to be confident or assured of, confide in, believe, trust, place or put confidence in; rely upon
la:verb:confido.html:
con-fīdo, fīsus sum, 3,
v. n., to trust confidently in something, confide in, rely firmly upon, to believe, be assured of (as an enhancing of sperare, ; ; freq. and class. in prose and poetry); constr. with abl., acc. and inf., with dat., rarely with de, ut, or absol.
With abl. (in verb. finit. very rare with personal object): aut corporis firmitate aut fortunae stabilitate,: copiā et facultate causae,; : illum, quo antea confidebant, metuunt,; : naturā loci,; ; : castrorum propinquitate,fin.; 3, 83; Lentul. ap. : jurejurando,; cf.: neque milites alio duce plus confidere aut audere,: socio Ulixe, (v. also under γ).—So esp. with part. pass.: confisus, a, um: neque Caesar opus intermittit confisus praesidio legionum trium,; ; ; Auct. B. Alex. 10, 5, Auct. B. G. 8, 3; 8, 15; Auct. B. Afr. 49: tam potenti duce confisus,; : nullā aliā urbe,; Lentul. : patientiā nostrā,: senatus consulto,.—

la:verb:confero#2.html:
confĕro, contŭli, collātum (conl-), conferre, v. a.
To bring, bear, or carry together, to collect, gather (freq. and class.).
In gen.: ligna circa casam,: arma,: cibos ore suo (aves),: undique collatis membris,: sarcinas in unum locum,; cf. : collatis militaribus signis,: ut premerer sacrā Lauroque collatāque myrto,: quo (sc. in proximum horreum) omne rusticum instrumentum,: illuc (sc. in castella) parentes et conjuges,: dentes in corpore (canes),: materiam omnem, antequam dicere ordiamur,: summas (scriptorum) in commentarium et capita,: plura opera in unam tabulam,: quae in proximos quinque libros conlata sunt,: res Romanas Graeco peregrinoque sermone in historiam, Just. pr. 1; cf. ; cf. I. B. 5. infra.; : rogus inimicis collatus manibus,—
In partic.
To collect money, treasures, etc., for any object, to bring offerings, contribute: dona mihi,: contulit aes populus,; so freq. on monuments: AERE CONLATO,; ; : EX AERE CONLATO,: aurum argentumque in publicum,: munera ei,: tributa quotannis ex censu,: conferre eo minus tributi,: in commune,; : quadringena talenta quotannis Delum,: (pecunia) ad ejus honores conlata,: ad honorem tuum pecunias maximas contulisse,: sextantes in capita,: pecunias,; ; ; : vinum alius, alius mel,; pr.: sua bona in medium, pr.: magnam partem patrimonii alicui rei,: cum et Socrati collatum sit ad victum,.—Absol.: nos dabimus, nos conferemus, nostro sumptu, non tuo,.—Hence,
Trop., like the Gr. συμφέρω (v. Lidd. and Scott in h. v. 5.), to be useful, profitable, to profit, serve, be of use to ( = prosum; cf. also conduco, II.; post-Aug., and only in the third person; most freq. in Quint.); constr. with ad, in, the dat., inf., or absol.
With ad: naturane plus ad eloquentiam conferat an doctrina,; so ; ; ; ; , prooem. § 6; .—*
With in: rursus in alia plus prior (exercitatio) confert,.—
With dat.: Gracchorum eloquentiae multum contulisse matrem,; so id. prooem. § 6; 2, 9, 2; 3, 7, 12 al.; ; ; ; .—
With subj. inf.: incipiente incremento confert alterna folia circum obruere,.—(ε) Absol.: multum veteres etiam Latini conferunt, imprimis copiam verborum,; ; ; cf. Sillig ad .—
To bring into connection, to unite, join, connect: membris collatis, of an embrace,; cf. ora,: fontes e quibus collatae aquae flumen emittunt,: capita, to lay heads together (in conferring, deliberating, etc.), ; : pedem, to go or come with one, ; so, gradum ( = congredi),; ; .—Of chemical union: dissimiles et dispares res in unam potestatem,.—
Trop.: collatis viribus,; cf.: conferre vires in unum,: collata omnium vota in unius salutem,: e singulis frustis collata oratio,; cf. : velut studia inter nos conferebamus,.— So esp. of conferences, consultations, etc., to consult together, confer, consider or talk over together: si quid res feret, coram inter nos conferemus,: sollicitudines nostras inter nos,: rationes,: familiares sermones cum aliquo, to unite in familiar conversation with, : cum hoc in viā sermonem contulit,; cf.: cum aliquo aut sermones aut consilia,: consilia ad adulescentes,; cf.: consilia dispersim antea habita,: injurias,to deliberate together concerning,; Cael. ap. .— Absol.: omnes sapientes decet conferre et fabulari,.—With a rel.clause: fusi contulerimus inter nos ... quid finis,: ibi conferentibus, quid animorum Hispanis esset,.—
To bring or join together in a hostile manner, to set together (most freq. in milit. lang.): (Galli) cum Fontejo ferrum ac manus contulerunt, (1, 2): signa cum Alexandrinis,; cf.: collatis signis depugnare,; : arma cum aliquo,; ; cf.: arma inter se,: castra cum hoste,; cf.: castra castris,; ; ; : pedem cum pede,to fight foot to foot,; cf.: pede conlato,; ; : gradum cum aliquo,: pectora luctantia nexu pectoribus,: stat conferre manum Aeneae,: prima movet Cacus collatā proelia dextrā,: collatis cursibus hastas conicere,: seque viro vir contulit,.—Poet.: inter sese duri certamina belli,: contra conferre manu certamina pugnae,: collato Marte,.—Absol.: mecum confer, ait,fight with me,.—
Transf. from milit. affairs to lawsuits: pedem, to encounter, come in contact with one, to attack: non possum magis pedem conferre, ut aiunt, aut propius accedere?: pedem cum singulis,; cf. ; cf.: qui illi concedi putem utilius esse quod postulat quam signa conferri,.—Poet.: lites,to contend, quarrel,.—
To bring together for comparison, to compare; constr. with cum, inter se, ad, the dat., or acc. only.
With cum: quem cum eo (sc. Democrito) conferre possumus non modo ingenii magnitudine sed etiam animi?; so : ut non conferam vitam neque existimationem tuam cum illius,, § 45; : cum maximis minima,; ; : nostras leges cum illorum Lycurgo et Dracone et Solone,; cf.: illa cum Graeciā,; v. also δ. —
With inter se (rare): vitam inter se utriusque conferte,.— *
With ad: bos ad bovem collatus, Müll.—
With dat.: tempora praesentia praeteritis,: parva magnis,: alicui illud,: lanam tinctam Tyriae lacernae,: ingenia ingeniis,: illam puellis,; : nil jucundo amico,: (Pausanias et Lysander) ne minimā quidem ex parte Lycurgi legibus et disciplinae conferendi sunt,; cf. supra, α.—(ε) With acc. only: tesseram hospitalem,: conferte Verrem: non ut hominem cum homine comparetis, etc.,: exemplum,; ; : nec cum quaereretur gener Tarquinio, quisquam Romanae juventutis ullā arte conferri potuit,; : census,.—Of documents: haec omnia summā curā et diligentiā recognita et conlata sunt,.—
With the idea of shortening by bringing together (cf. colligo), to compress, abridge, condense, make or be brief: quam potero in verba conferam paucissima,; cf.: in pauca, ut occupatus nunc sum, confer, quid velis,: rem in pauca,; and: in pauca verba,; id: : totam Academiam ... ex duobus libris contuli in quattuor,: ut in pauca conferam,: sua verba in duos versus,: ex immensā diffusāque legum copiā optima quaeque et necessaria in paucissimos libros,.—

*

To join in bringing forward, to propose unitedly (as a law; cf. fero, II. B. 8. b.): cur enim non confertis, ne sit conubium divitibus et pauperibus, Weissenb. ad loc.
(Con intens.) To bear, carry, convey, direct a thing somewhere (in haste, for protection, etc.); and conferre se, to betake or turn one's self anywhere, to go (very freq. and class.).
Prop.
In gen.
With the designation of the goal: quo me miser conferam? Gracch. ap. : qui cum se suaque omnia in oppidum Bratuspantium contulissent,: se suaque eo,: se suaque in naves,: iter Brundisium versus,; cf.: iter eo, Brut. ap. : suas rationes et copias in illam provinciam,: legiones in mediam aciem, Auct. B. Alex. 39; Auct. B. Afr. 60: quos eodem audita Cannensis clades contulerat,: parentes illuc,: se Rhodum conferre,: se Laodiceam, Lent. ap. : se Colonas,: quo se fusa acies,: se ad Tissaphernem,; so, se ad Pharnabazum,: se in fugam,: sese in pedes, Enn. ap. ; (cf.: conicere se in pedes,).—Of things: pituita eo se umorve confert,.—
Absol.: pulcre haec confertur ratis,is borne away,.—
Esp., in (cf. abeo, II.): aliquem in aliquid, to change into, transform to something: aliquem in saxum,: versos vultus (poet. circumlocution for se) in hanc, : corpus in albam volucrem,.—
Trop.
In gen., to bring, turn, direct something to; and conferre se, to turn, apply, devote one's self to, etc.: quo mortuo me ad pontificem Scaevolam contuli,: (Crassus) cum initio aetatis ad amicitiam se meam contulisset,; : qui se ad senatūs auctoritatem, ad libertatem vestram contulerunt,; : se ad studium scribendi,: se ad studia litterarum,; cf. : meus pater eam seditionem in tranquillum conferet (the figure taken from the sea when in commotion),: verba ad rem, to bring words to actions, i. e. to pass from words to deeds, ; : suspitionem in Capitonem,: ut spes votaque sua non prius ad deos quam ad principum aures conferret,: lamentationes suas etiam in testamentum,.—More freq., in partic.,
With the access. idea of application or communication, to devote or apply something to a certain purpose, to employ, direct, confer, bestow upon, give, lend, grant, to transfer to (a favorite word with Cic.).
With dat.: dona quid cessant mihi Conferre?: tibi munera,; : victoribus praemia,: puellae quinquaginta milia nummūm,: fructum alio,; .—
With ad and acc.: hostiles exuvias ornatum ad urbis et posterum gloriam,: Mithridates omne reliquum tempus non ad oblivionem veteris belli, sed ad comparationem novi contulit,: omne studium atque omne ingenium ad populi Romani gloriam laudemque celebrandam,; : omnem meam curam atque operam ad philosophiam,: omnem tuum amorem omnemque tuam prudentiam ... confer ad eam curam,: animum ad fodiendos puteos, Auct. B. Alex. 9: ad naturae suae non vitiosae genus consilium vivendi omne,: orationem omnem ad misericordiam,.—
With in: omnes curas cogitationesque in rem publicam,: diligentiam in valetudinem tuam,: praedas ac manubias suas non in monumenta deorum immortalium, neque in urbis ornamenta conferre, sed, etc.,: in eos, quos speramus nobis profuturos, non dubitamus officia conferre,; so, plurimum benignitatis in eum,; : curam restituendi Capitolii in L. Vestinum confert, i. e. assigns to, charges with, : in unius salutem collata omnium vota,.—
With erga: commemoratio benevolentiae ejus, quam erga me a pueritiā contulisses,.—
With aliquid ad or in aliquem or aliquid, to refer or ascribe something to a person or thing as its possessor, author (in a good, and freq. in a bad sense), to attribute, impute, assign, ascribe to one, to lay to the charge of: species istas hominum in deos,: res ad imperium deorum,: permulta in Plancium, quae ab eo numquam dicta sunt, conferuntur ... Stomachor vero, cum aliorum non me digna in me conferuntur,; : mortis illius invidiam in L. Flaccum,: suum timorem in rei frumentariae simulationem angustiasque itinerum,: sua vitia et suam culpam in senectutem,: hanc ego de re publicā disputationem in Africani personam et Phili contuli,.—So esp.: culpam in aliquem,; ; , a, 1: causam in aliquem,; ; cf.: causam in tempus,.—
To transfer to a fixed point of time, fix, assign, refer, appoint, put off, defer, postpone (cf. differo): Carthaginis expugnationem in hunc annum,: in posterum diem iter suum contulit, Brut. ap. : omnia in mensem Martium,: aliquid in ambulationis tempus,: eam pecuniam in rei publicae magnum aliquod tempus,: quod in longiorem diem conlaturus fuisset,: alicujus consulatum in annum aliquem,.—Rarely of place: idoneum locum in agris nactus ... ibi adventum expectare Pompei eoque omnem belli rationem conferre constituit,—
To bring on, cause, occasion, induce: pestem alicui,: candorem mollitiamque,.
